title: AF-1-part-3
description: Airframe exam covering aircraft weight and balance: CG computation, moment/arm, loading graphs, ballast, adverse-loaded CG checks, weighing procedures, and related regulatory/documentation requirements, drawn from the AF-1 weight and balance question/answer bank.

questions.question: Baggage weighing 50 lb is moved from aft station 246 to forward station 118 on an aircraft weighing 4,706 lb. What happens to the CG?
options: A. The CG moves aft 1.36 inches
B. The CG moves forward 1.36 inches
C. The CG does not change
questions.explanation: Moving weight forward shifts the CG forward; the shift equals (weight moved x distance moved)/total weight = (50 x 128)/4706 ≈ 1.36 inches forward.

questions.question: Which document is used to determine the maximum weight allowed for an aircraft under given altitude, temperature, wind, and runway conditions?
options: A. The aircraft's weight and balance record only
B. The Pilot's Operating Handbook (POH) or Airplane Flight Manual (AFM)
C. The maintenance logbook
questions.explanation: Performance-limited maximum weights for specific conditions (altitude, temperature, wind, runway) are found in the POH/AFM performance charts.

questions.question: Which of the following does NOT call for a weight and balance check?
options: A. Installation of new equipment
B. A routine preflight check
C. A major repair or alteration
questions.explanation: A routine preflight walk-around does not itself require a new weight and balance computation; that is driven by changes in configuration or loading, not daily preflight.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT an effect of overloading an aircraft?
options: A. Inefficient movement of control surfaces
B. Reduced climb performance
C. Reduced range
questions.explanation: Overloading primarily degrades performance (climb, range, ceiling) and structural margins; it does not directly cause inefficient control surface movement.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a requirement checked during a weight and balance check?
options: A. Total weight within maximum limits
B. Weight accumulated near the CG
C. CG within forward and aft limits
questions.explanation: Weight and balance checks confirm total weight and CG position are within limits; where the weight happens to be relative to the CG is not itself a pass/fail requirement.

questions.question: What is an effect of aircraft overload?
options: A. Increased cruise speed
B. Increased service ceiling
C. Decreased cruise speed and range
questions.explanation: An overloaded aircraft requires more power to maintain altitude and speed, resulting in reduced cruise speed, range, and ceiling.

questions.question: What should be done while preparing an aircraft for weighing?
options: A. Fill the fuel tanks completely
B. Load maximum baggage
C. Drain the oil (per the weighing procedure/empty weight definition)
questions.explanation: Weighing procedures typically call for draining items such as engine oil per the empty weight definition used, so the aircraft is weighed in a standard configuration.

questions.question: A CG located slightly ahead of the center of lift produces what tendency?
options: A. A fixed nose-up pitching tendency
B. No pitching tendency at all
C. A fixed nose-down pitching tendency, independent of aircraft attitude
questions.explanation: With the CG forward of the center of lift, the aircraft has an inherent nose-down tendency that contributes to longitudinal (pitch) stability.

questions.question: Where is permanent ballast typically located on an aircraft?
options: A. As close to the CG as possible
B. Only in the wing root
C. At the extremes, forward or aft
questions.explanation: Permanent ballast is placed at the forward or aft extremes of the aircraft to most effectively shift the empty weight CG back within limits.

questions.question: In computing weight and balance, a station located aft of the datum is considered what?
options: A. Positive
B. Negative
C. Zero
questions.explanation: By convention, stations measured aft of the datum are positive, while those forward of the datum are negative.

questions.question: How does increasing the moment arm affect the moment, for a given weight?
options: A. It decreases the moment
B. It has no effect on the moment
C. It increases the moment
questions.explanation: Moment = weight x arm, so for a fixed weight, increasing the arm (distance from datum) increases the resulting moment.

questions.question: What is an effect of having the aircraft's weight too far forward?
options: A. Increased elevator authority for takeoff rotation
B. No effect on elevator authority
C. Reduced elevator authority for takeoff rotation
questions.explanation: A very forward CG increases the nose-down moment the elevator must overcome, reducing available elevator authority for rotation at takeoff.

questions.question: Which of the following is caused by overloading an aircraft?
options: A. The service ceiling will be lowered
B. The service ceiling will be raised
C. The stall speed will decrease
questions.explanation: Excess weight reduces the altitude at which the aircraft can maintain a given climb rate, lowering its service ceiling.

questions.question: Pressure altitude corrected for non-standard temperature is called what?
options: A. Indicated altitude
B. True altitude
C. Density altitude
questions.explanation: Density altitude is pressure altitude adjusted for temperature deviation from the standard atmosphere.

questions.question: When the CG is found to be at or near its limit (out of range or borderline), what must be performed?
options: A. A routine preflight inspection only
B. A fuel dump procedure
C. An adverse-loaded CG check
questions.explanation: When CG is near its limits, an adverse-loaded CG check verifies the aircraft remains within limits under worst-case (forward/aft) loading scenarios.

questions.question: Payload consists of the load of what?
options: A. Fuel and oil only
B. Cargo and passengers
C. Crew only
questions.explanation: Payload is the revenue-producing load carried by the aircraft, namely passengers and cargo, as distinct from fuel, oil, or crew.

questions.question: Which of the following is true regarding weight and balance requirements?
options: A. Weight and balance limits never apply to private aircraft
B. Weight and balance is only required for aircraft over 12,500 lb
C. It is not mandatory for every private owner-pilot flight in the same way airline operations are regulated, but limits must still be respected
questions.explanation: While formal documentation requirements can differ by operation type, every aircraft must still be operated within its certificated weight and balance limits.

questions.question: The Pilot's Operating Handbook (POH) typically contains which weight and balance information?
options: A. A loading graph and CG moment envelope
B. Engine overhaul schedules only
C. Airspace chart data
questions.explanation: The POH includes weight and balance data such as loading graphs and CG/moment envelopes to help compute a safe loading condition.

questions.question: What is load factor?
options: A. The ratio of the maximum load an aircraft can sustain to the total weight of the aircraft
B. The ratio of fuel weight to empty weight
C. The ratio of wing area to total weight
questions.explanation: Load factor expresses the load the structure can sustain (in g's) as a multiple of the aircraft's weight.

questions.question: What happens if an aircraft is overloaded?
options: A. Both angle of climb and rate of climb decrease
B. Both angle of climb and rate of climb increase
C. Only cruise speed is affected
questions.explanation: Excess weight reduces the excess thrust/power available for climbing, decreasing both the climb angle and climb rate.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT true during overloading?
options: A. Takeoff distance increases
B. Cruise speed increases
C. Stall speed increases
questions.explanation: Overloading increases stall speed and takeoff distance while decreasing performance; cruise speed does not increase as a result of overload.

questions.question: Weight, arm, and moment used to compute the loaded weight and CG define what?
options: A. The graphical method
B. The index method
C. The computational method
questions.explanation: The computational (tabular) method uses weight x arm = moment calculations for each item to determine total weight and CG.

questions.question: In computing weight and balance, a station located forward of the datum is considered what?
options: A. Positive
B. Negative
C. Zero
questions.explanation: By convention, stations forward of the datum are negative, and those aft of the datum are positive.

questions.question: Under what condition would fuel dumping be appropriate?
options: A. Whenever the fuel tanks are more than half full
B. When there is excess fuel and the aircraft must return before burning it off normally (e.g., an emergency return)
C. Only during normal scheduled landings
questions.explanation: Fuel dumping is used when an aircraft must land at a weight below its maximum landing weight sooner than normal fuel burn would allow, such as an emergency return shortly after takeoff.

questions.question: "Aircraft Nose Up (ANU)" and percentage of MAC relate to what setting?
options: A. The flap setting
B. The stabilizer trim setting
C. The autopilot mode
questions.explanation: Takeoff stabilizer trim settings are often expressed in "units ANU" correlated to the CG position as a percentage of MAC.

questions.question: When an aircraft maneuvers smoothly and sharply at a 60-degree bank angle, what happens to the load?
options: A. The dynamic load stays at 1g
B. The dynamic load should be about twice the normal (1g) load
C. The dynamic load becomes negative
questions.explanation: A level 60-degree banked turn imposes a load factor of about 2g, roughly double the normal 1g load.

questions.question: If an item is shifted forward in the aircraft, what happens to the CG?
options: A. The CG moves forward (its arm decreases)
B. The CG moves aft
C. The CG is unaffected
questions.explanation: Moving weight forward reduces the average moment arm, shifting the overall CG forward.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT considered part of tare weight?
options: A. Wheel chocks on the scale
B. Jacks or stands supporting the aircraft on the scale
C. A wheel fairing (permanently installed part)
questions.explanation: Tare weight covers temporary items used to support/position the aircraft for weighing, such as chocks and jacks; a permanently installed wheel fairing is part of the aircraft, not tare.

questions.question: If a 50 lb weight is shifted to a point 2 m aft of the current CG, what happens to the CG limit?
options: A. The CG shifts forward
B. The CG limit is unaffected
C. The CG shifts aft
questions.explanation: Shifting weight aft of the existing CG moves the overall center of gravity rearward.

questions.question: What is the load factor limit commonly specified for a utility category aircraft?
questions.explanation: Utility category aircraft are typically certificated for load factors around +4.4g, higher than the +3.8g typical of normal category aircraft.

questions.question: What is the enclosed area on a graph of the airplane's loaded weight versus loaded moment called?
options: A. The performance chart
B. The loading schedule
C. The CG moment envelope
questions.explanation: The CG/moment envelope is the graphed region showing all combinations of weight and moment (or CG) that are within approved limits.

questions.question: For an aircraft to have proper flight characteristics, where should the CG generally be located?
options: A. At the trailing edge of the chord
B. Near the leading edge of the mean aerodynamic chord, within the approved range
C. Behind the center of lift at all times
questions.explanation: The CG must fall within the approved range, generally near the forward portion of the chord relative to the center of lift, for proper stability and control.

questions.question: What is the purpose of determining CG relative to the Mean Aerodynamic Chord (MAC)?
options: A. To calculate fuel burn rate
B. To express CG position relative to the wing chord for comparison with approved limits
C. To determine engine thrust required
questions.explanation: Expressing CG as a percentage of MAC standardizes CG position relative to the wing's aerodynamic reference chord, matching the format of approved CG limits.

questions.question: Which of the following is critical for calculating the landing weight of large aircraft?
options: A. Determining the minutes of fuel dump time (or fuel burn) needed to reach landing weight
B. The color of the exterior paint
C. The cabin lighting configuration
questions.explanation: For large aircraft, the time to burn off or dump fuel to reach an acceptable landing weight is a critical calculation for return-to-land scenarios.

questions.question: What is vital in the weight and balance consideration of an aircraft?
options: A. The aircraft must always be loaded to maximum weight
B. The CG must always be at the aft limit
C. The total weight of the aircraft must not be greater than the maximum allowable weight
questions.explanation: The fundamental weight and balance requirement is that total weight stays at or below the certificated maximum, with CG within approved limits.

questions.question: Which statement is true regarding weighing an aircraft?
options: A. It must always be done outdoors for accuracy
B. It must be done in a hangar, with fuel and oil not considered part of empty weight drained per the applicable procedure
C. Fuel tanks must be completely full
questions.explanation: Weighing is performed indoors (to avoid wind effects) with the aircraft configured per the empty weight definition, draining fluids not included in empty weight.

questions.question: Who is responsible for the weight and balance check after a 100-hour inspection?
options: A. Any licensed pilot
B. Someone holding inspection authorization (or otherwise appropriately certificated/authorized)
C. The aircraft owner only
questions.explanation: Verifying weight and balance as part of required inspections is the responsibility of appropriately authorized maintenance personnel, such as an IA holder.

questions.question: While calculating weight and balance, tare weight must be handled how relative to the scale reading?
options: A. Subtracted from the scale reading
B. Added to the scale reading
C. Multiplied by the scale reading
questions.explanation: Tare weight (chocks, jacks, etc.) is subtracted from the gross scale reading to get the actual aircraft weight at that point.

questions.question: How do you determine the distance of the CG behind LEMAC (Leading Edge of the Mean Aerodynamic Chord)?
options: A. By subtracting the distance between the datum and LEMAC from the distance between the datum and the CG
B. By adding the distance between the datum and the CG to the MAC length
C. By dividing the CG moment by the MAC length
questions.explanation: Distance of CG aft of LEMAC = (datum-to-CG distance) minus (datum-to-LEMAC distance).

questions.question: Which of the following is correct regarding the weighing scale used for large aircraft?
options: A. Any bathroom-type scale is acceptable
B. Calibration is optional if the scale looks undamaged
C. The weighing scale must be calibrated before use
questions.explanation: Large aircraft weighing requires scales that are properly calibrated to ensure accurate weight and balance data.

questions.question: At what flight phase is the stabilizer trim limit typically referenced/set?
options: A. Takeoff
B. Cruise
C. Taxi
questions.explanation: Stabilizer trim settings for takeoff are determined based on CG position (percent MAC) and are a critical pre-takeoff configuration item.

questions.question: What is used to determine if an aircraft is properly loaded for its flight?
options: A. The fuel burn chart
B. The engine performance chart
C. The CG limit envelope
questions.explanation: The CG limit (moment) envelope shows whether the computed weight and CG combination falls within the approved safe loading region.

questions.question: Who is responsible for weight and balance control of an aircraft?
options: A. Only the aircraft manufacturer
B. The pilot who operates it and the Aviation Maintenance Technician (AMT) who maintains it
C. Only air traffic control
questions.explanation: Both the operating pilot (proper loading) and the maintaining AMT (accurate records/empty weight data) share responsibility for weight and balance control.

questions.question: What is the purpose of computing weight and balance before flight?
options: A. To determine fuel price
B. To determine the CG location relative to its limits
C. To determine engine oil pressure
questions.explanation: Pre-flight weight and balance computation confirms the loaded CG falls within approved forward and aft limits for safe flight.

questions.question: What is needed after a repair or alteration has moved the empty CG outside its limits, typically made of lead blocks painted red?
options: A. Temporary ballast
B. A tare weight adjustment
C. Permanent ballast
questions.explanation: Permanent ballast (often lead blocks painted red for identification) is installed to bring the empty weight CG back within its approved limits.

questions.question: Which of the following will have the maximum value among typical aircraft weights?
options: A. Maximum takeoff weight
B. Empty weight
C. Maximum zero-fuel weight
questions.explanation: Maximum takeoff weight (which includes fuel) is generally the largest of the standard weight limits for a given aircraft.

questions.question: Which is the correct condition for weighing an aircraft regarding engine oil?
options: A. The oil tank must be completely full
B. The oil level does not matter for weighing
C. The oil tank should be empty, accounting for residual (undrainable) fluid as specified
questions.explanation: Weighing procedures specify the oil condition (often drained, with residual undrainable oil accounted for) consistent with the empty weight definition used.

questions.question: Where would you find the equipment list used to update the weight and balance record?
options: A. The flight plan
B. The Pilot's Operating Handbook (POH)
C. The maintenance release only
questions.explanation: The equipment list, which tracks installed items affecting empty weight and CG, is typically found in or referenced by the POH/AFM weight and balance section.

questions.question: What is tare weight?
options: A. The weight of fuel remaining after a flight
B. The weight of the crew and baggage
C. The weight of chocks or any device used to hold the aircraft on the scale
questions.explanation: Tare weight is the weight of items (chocks, jacks, etc.) used to support or position the aircraft during weighing that must be subtracted from the reading.

questions.question: What is the center of gravity of an aircraft when it contains only the items specified in its empty weight?
options: A. Basic operating CG
B. Zero-fuel CG
C. Empty Weight CG (EWCG)
questions.explanation: Empty Weight CG is the CG location of the aircraft in its empty weight configuration, before adding crew, payload, and usable fuel.

questions.question: Longitudinal stability is maintained by ensuring what relationship between CG and center of lift?
options: A. The CG is slightly ahead of the center of lift
B. The CG is well behind the center of lift
C. The CG coincides exactly with the center of lift
questions.explanation: A CG slightly forward of the center of lift creates a stabilizing nose-down tendency that contributes to positive longitudinal stability.

questions.question: Aircraft structures, in the context of weight and balance moments, can be considered as what?
options: A. A hydraulic system
B. A pure truss with no moments
C. A first-class lever
questions.explanation: The weight-arm-moment relationship used in weight and balance treats the aircraft like a first-class lever balanced about the datum/CG.

questions.question: Which is a correct condition for weighing an aircraft regarding the fuel tanks?
options: A. Fuel tanks must be completely full
B. Fuel tanks should be empty, with only residual (hanging) fluid as specified by procedure
C. Fuel tanks should be half full
questions.explanation: Weighing is normally done with fuel drained per the empty weight definition, leaving only unusable/residual fluid.

questions.question: A check where the forward CG limit is loaded to its maximum and the aft limit is loaded to its minimum describes what?
options: A. An aft adverse-loaded CG check
B. A routine weighing
C. A forward adverse-loaded CG check
questions.explanation: A forward adverse-loaded CG check verifies the airplane remains safely controllable when loaded to produce the most forward possible CG.

questions.question: A check where the rearward CG limit is loaded to its maximum and the forward limit is loaded to its minimum describes what?
options: A. A forward adverse-loaded CG check
B. A routine weighing
C. An aft adverse-loaded CG check
questions.explanation: An aft adverse-loaded CG check verifies the airplane remains safely controllable when loaded to produce the most aft possible CG.

questions.question: Ballast that is needed only for certain flight conditions and is often found in sandbag form is called what?
options: A. Permanent ballast
B. Structural ballast
C. Temporary ballast
questions.explanation: Temporary ballast, such as sandbags, is added or removed as needed for specific loading conditions, unlike permanently installed ballast.

questions.question: Whose responsibility is it to update the weight and balance record after any major repair or modification?
options: A. The passenger
B. The repairman (performing/certifying the work)
C. Air traffic control
questions.explanation: The person performing and certifying a major repair or modification is responsible for updating the aircraft's weight and balance record to reflect the change.

questions.question: How is weight and balance typically computed on modern (large transport) aircraft?
options: A. By a dedicated flight electronic computer (e.g., an onboard weight and balance/load system)
B. By manual slide-rule calculation only
C. It is not computed on modern aircraft
questions.explanation: Modern large aircraft often use dedicated electronic systems to compute weight and balance automatically from loaded weights and positions.

questions.question: What is the first step in calculating an aircraft's empty weight from scale readings?
options: A. Calculate the CG location
B. Determine the net weight at each wheel/scale position
C. Look up the maximum takeoff weight
questions.explanation: Empty weight calculation starts by recording and net-ing (after subtracting tare) the weight measured at each wheel/jack point.

questions.question: Which method uses a weight and moment index for calculating weight and balance?
options: A. The computational (tabular) method
B. The loading graph method
C. The direct scale-reading method
questions.explanation: The loading graph method uses index units (scaled moments) plotted on a graph to quickly determine total weight and CG without lengthy arithmetic.

questions.question: Lateral balance of an aircraft is most affected by what?
options: A. Cabin temperature
B. Outside air pressure
C. Fuel usage (asymmetric tank depletion)
questions.explanation: Uneven fuel burn between left and right tanks can shift the lateral CG, which is why lateral balance is primarily a function of fuel usage/management.

questions.question: How do you shift the CG back within its limit if it is found out of range?
options: A. By adding more fuel regardless of tank
B. By shifting passenger and/or cargo load
C. By reducing airspeed
questions.explanation: An out-of-limits CG is corrected operationally by repositioning passengers and/or cargo to bring the CG back within approved limits.

questions.question: Where would you typically find a loading graph for an aircraft?
options: A. In the maintenance logbook
B. In the Pilot's Operating Handbook (POH)
C. In the type certificate data sheet only
questions.explanation: Loading graphs used for quick weight and balance computation are published in the aircraft's POH/AFM.

questions.question: What is the purpose of computing weight and balance before flight (regarding load)?
options: A. To determine the minimum crew required
B. To determine required runway lighting
C. To determine the maximum allowable load for that flight
questions.explanation: Weight and balance computation before flight confirms how much load (fuel, passengers, cargo) can be carried while staying within limits.

questions.question: Which of the following speeds up the preflight weight and balance computation?
options: A. The long-hand computational method
B. Re-weighing the aircraft before every flight
C. The loading graph method
questions.explanation: The loading graph method lets pilots quickly read weight and moment values from a chart, speeding up preflight calculations compared with manual computation.

questions.question: Which of the following is correct about weight and balance records?
options: A. All weight and balance records should be kept with the other aircraft records
B. Weight and balance records may be discarded after each flight
C. Weight and balance records are optional for certificated aircraft
questions.explanation: Weight and balance records, including the equipment list and latest computations, must be maintained as part of the aircraft's permanent records.

questions.question: Given CG location 635.7, LEMAC station 625, and MAC of 134, what is the distance from the CG to LEMAC expressed as a percentage of MAC?
options: A. 15% (20.1 inches)
B. 8% (10.7 inches)
C. 4% (5.4 inches)
questions.explanation: Distance behind LEMAC = 635.7 - 625 = 10.7 inches; as a percentage of MAC: 10.7/134 ≈ 8%.

questions.question: Which weighing equipment is used for light aircraft, requiring a ramp and jack to place the aircraft on the scale?
options: A. A mechanical platform scale
B. A portable electronic weighing system
C. A load cell under each wheel only
questions.explanation: Mechanical platform scales for light aircraft often require ramps/jacks to position the aircraft's wheels onto the scale platforms.

questions.question: Weight added to an aircraft is considered what, for moment calculation purposes?
options: A. Negative
B. Zero
C. Positive
questions.explanation: Adding weight contributes a positive moment value when computing the change in total moment for weight and balance purposes.

questions.question: The load imposed on an aircraft structure due to the weight of the aircraft and its contents is called what?
options: A. Static load
B. Dynamic load
C. Aerodynamic load
questions.explanation: Static load refers to the load from the aircraft's own weight and contents, as opposed to dynamic loads from maneuvering or gusts.

questions.question: What is the formula for determining the CG of an aircraft?
options: A. Total moment divided by total weight
B. Total weight divided by total moment
C. Total weight multiplied by total arm
questions.explanation: CG location = total moment / total weight, derived from the sum of each item's weight x arm divided by the sum of weights.

questions.question: Which weighing equipment is used for both large and small aircraft, has its own ramp, and provides digital CG and gross-weight readouts?
options: A. A mechanical platform scale
B. A fixed hangar floor scale
C. A portable electronic weighing system
questions.explanation: Portable electronic weighing systems include their own ramps and digital readouts for gross weight and CG, suitable for aircraft of various sizes.

questions.question: Whose responsibility is it to update the aircraft's new empty weight when there is a change in the equipment list?
options: A. The passenger
B. Air traffic control
C. The operator
questions.explanation: The aircraft operator is responsible for ensuring the empty weight and equipment list are updated whenever installed equipment changes.
